predecessors.name: Zhou dynasty
predecessors.text: Zeng, 'territory in the area around Suizhou in modern Hubei province' (findings 'reached up to the south west border of Henan province')

successors.name: Chu
successors.text: Zeng, 'territory in the area around Suizhou in modern Hubei province' (findings 'reached up to the south west border of Henan province')

ledger.x: c. 1045: Zeng is enfeoffed at Suizhou. 'founded during the time of Western Zhou (1045 - 771 BC)'; descendants of Nangong Kuo 'enfeoffed in Suizhou to pacify the local Huaiyi tribes'. The page dates no year within the span, so the span's first year is a bridge.
5th century BC: the state of Zeng ends in Chu's annexation; year not on the page.

wars.name: Chu-Zeng wars
wars.outcome: King Wu of Chu invaded Zeng in 706 and attacked again in 704 (Zeng lost the Battle of Suqi, peace followed that year); Wu died on an expedition into Zeng in 690; in 640 the vassals led by Zeng attacked Chu and were beaten; after Chengpu (632) 'Zeng was…

certainty.note: No Zeng boundary is on the page; soft throughout.
